statement: Split the per-node projection-readiness contract into (1) an immutable timestamp-free SEMANTIC CORE owned per node by the evidence owner — normalized/frozen exactly once per (node, semantic generation), with a generation key that digests ONLY semantic dependencies: table mutation versions, planning version, and transport/lifecycle/publication/repair verdict CONTENT with per-evaluation observation-time fields excluded after an explicit classified inventory — and (2) a fresh per-evaluation ENVELOPE owned by the evaluation-snapshot layer that carries this call's observation-time metadata. Invariants: same node + unchanged semantic generation across clock-advancing evaluations => exactly one semantic-core normalization and the SAME immutable core reference (ENGAGEMENT — a mutation that returns observation time to the semantic key must red the receipt); every evaluation still observes through SourceObservationOwner under its existing freshness contract, and its envelope/snapshot carries THAT call's observedAt (FRESHNESS — reuse never makes a consumer-visible freshness field stale); each actual semantic dependency change rotates the core while a moving clock alone never does (SEMANTIC-KEY); cores remain strictly per-node (no cross-node sharing, preserving the falsified-cluster-share finding); the semantic key never decides whether an authoritative read occurs (SourceObservationOwner authority untouched); no cached core is ever mutated to refresh timestamps — envelopes are new small objects; consumer-visible contract compatibility is preserved through the owned snapshot/adapter projection, not by consumers understanding the split. Effectiveness is proven by a local engagement profile (order 10k evaluations under tens of semantic generations => tens of core builds, ~99% core reuse, normalize/strict-own-data/allocation costs measurably moved), not by semantic tests alone.
